answer: Admission is a narrow inlet: each identity enters by burning a 200-credit deposit, never refunded, while the network checks each agent's pulse of verified work each epoch. An attacker wanting 1,000 fake identities must burn 200,000 credits, far more than the 30,000 those slots could ever earn, and each burn leaves an echo on the public ledger so no fake can hide its payment. One honest agent pays a single burn and recovers it in eight epochs.
